title: Version module starting at 1.00 (guideline §8.1)
prompt:
Add a version module in packages/core (e.g. core/_version.py with __version__ = "1.00") and re-export it from the SDK package __init__. Add a test asserting the version is importable and starts at 1.00.

Follow repo standards: TDD (write the failing test first, then code); max 150 lines per code file (split, don't compress); ruff = 0 violations + mypy clean; no hard-coded values (read from config); every external API call goes through the API gatekeeper (Epic 13); log via the LOG package; keep coverage >= 85%. Read docs/PRD.md and the relevant docs/prds/*.md before starting.
note: TDD: wrote packages/core/tests/test_version.py FIRST with 4 assertions (`from agent_debate.core import __version__` importable and == '1.00'; __version__ is a MAJOR.MINOR numeric string via regex; the dedicated `_version` module exposes the canonical constant; LIBRARY_VERSION and core_version alias __version__ so there is no duplicate literal). Watched all 4 fail (ImportError/AttributeError, red), then implemented. Created packages/core/src/agent_debate/core/_version.py as the single source of truth (`__version__ = "1.00"`) and re-exported it from agent_debate.core's __init__, adding __version__ to __all__. Reconciliation: __version__ is now the source of truth; the pre-existing LIBRARY_VERSION and core_version aliases were changed from a hard-coded '1.00' literal to reference __version__, so the version string is defined in exactly one place. The per-package smoke tests (which assert LIBRARY_VERSION is a non-empty str) stay green unchanged. pyproject version fields already read '1.00' across all five packages and remain consistent with __version__ (dynamic version from code left as nice-to-have, not wired, to avoid contradiction). Gates green locally: ruff check, ruff format --check, mypy, pytest --cov (>=85), check_line_limit.py, secret_scan.py.
